rows.originalText: Punctuation is tested through underlined-segment error-spotting (a colon, semicolon, dash or apostrophe hidden among four options) and through "which sentence is punctuated correctly" MCQs, almost never through open punctuation-insertion. The classic trap is a mark that is legal in isolation but wrong for its neighbours — a colon straight after a verb, or one half of a matched pair (dash, bracket) present while the other half is silently swapped for a comma.
